query: Half the team says "booking" and the other half says "reservation", and the code uses both interchangeably. Can we settle on one and write it down somewhere?
The word "settlement window" keeps showing up in new code and nobody has defined it — two people clearly mean different things by it.
I want the terminology nailed down before we build anything: what exactly is an order versus a cart versus a checkout in this system?
We just decided that a subscription can never span two billing accounts. Capture that somewhere it won't get lost by next month.
Write up the decision we reached about soft deletes, including the options we rejected and why.
Our glossary file is badly out of date after the last three design sessions. Bring it back in line with what we actually decided.
As we work through these decision tickets one by one, keep the project's vocabulary and decision record updated as each one lands.
The spec and the database columns use different names for the same concept and it's causing real bugs. I want the language fixed first.
I'm about to rename half the core types. Before I do, let's agree on what each concept is actually called and record it.
How should I draw aggregate boundaries between orders and line items, and which one is the consistency boundary?
Is this a separate bounded context or just a module? I think we need an anticorruption layer between us and the legacy billing system.
Explain the difference between an entity and a value object, and when a factory is worth having.
Our deploy runbook is stale and the API reference is missing three endpoints we shipped last quarter.
This spec has no acceptance criteria. Write them so QA can actually verify the feature.
Should the business logic here live in a Transaction Script or a full Domain Model with a Unit of Work?
How do we evolve this event schema without breaking downstream consumers that are still on the old version?
Turn this whole conversation into a PRD and publish it to the tracker — no interview, just write up what we said.
Rename this variable and extract the duplicated block into a helper without changing behavior.
Set up pre-commit hooks so ruff and mypy run before every commit.
